### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A27, A28 and A29 each appear in only about 45–55% of traces, whereas before they appeared in every trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A20’s outgoing behaviour changed: before it was followed by A28 in about 47% of cases and A29 in about 53%; in the later window it is followed by A21 in all observed cases. [DIR001]
- A23’s outgoing behaviour changed: before it was always followed by A27; in the later window it is followed by A27 in about 45% of cases, A28 in about 30%, and A29 in about 25%. [DIR002]
- A28 and A29 no longer lead to A21; instead A28 is followed by A29 or A24, and A29 is followed by A24 or A28. [DIR003, DIR004]
- Ordering changed: A21 and A23 now precede A28 and A29 in the later window, whereas before A28 and A29 preceded them. [REL005, REL006, REL008, REL009]
- A27 no longer co-occurs with A28 or A29; the two groups appear in mutually exclusive subsets of traces. [REL013, REL014]
- A28 and A29 moved much closer to A24 and farther from A20 in terms of event positions. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG007, LAG008, POS006, POS007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the branch through A28/A29 was moved later in the process, while A21 and A23 became an earlier common path. Specifically, A20 now always leads to A21 instead of branching to A28/A29; A23 now branches to A27 or to A28/A29; A28/A29 now lead to A24 instead of back to A21; and A27 no longer appears together with A28/A29. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, REL013, REL014] The consistency of the successor, ordering, co-occurrence and position indicators makes it unlikely that this is only a sampling artefact, although finite variant frequencies cannot be completely ruled out as a competing explanation. [OCC001, DIR001, REL005, LAG007]
